answer: Identity enrollment starts with a memory-bus latency probe: the challenger writes a 4 GB basalt-pattern buffer across the agent's claimed RAM, then demands nanosecond-budget random reads inside a 40 ns window. Genuine silicon serves each read in ~12 ns; a spoofed identity multiplexed onto shared hardware shows skewed, fat-tailed latency. The verifier repeats the probe across a spiral of 64 offset addresses to defeat caching, and rejects any profile whose read jitter exceeds a velvet-smooth baseline by more than 3 sigma.
